solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Iron horse provided heads, cost of use varying regularly

indicators.note: to head something is to go in front of it, so the earlier pair of pieces is placed before the later pair

parts.note: an equid is any member of the horse family
provided, as in 'on condition that'
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron
rent is the price paid for using something

explanation.surface: A railway locomotive's fares seem to jump about in a regular pattern.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Iron horse' looks like a locomotive, but the two words part company: 'horse provided' heads, meaning goes in front of, 'Iron, cost of use'.
explanation.definitionFit: Equidifferent describes a series whose successive terms differ by the same amount, as in an arithmetic progression.

clue.text: One squeezing part held by Morse inventor with both leads cut off

indicators.note: leads are the front letters, and cutting them off strips the opening letter from each of the two words involved
to be held by something is to sit inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: Colin Dexter created Inspector Morse; his surname loses its first letter D
portion means a part; it loses its first letter P

explanation.surface: Someone who wrings things is caught up in the work of the man who gave us the Morse code.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Morse inventor' suggests Samuel Morse of the code, but it is Colin Dexter, author of the Inspector Morse novels.
explanation.definitionFit: An extortioner wrings money from victims by threats, squeezing them financially.

clue.text: Northerner's lonely bachelor banished from occupied bed

indicators.note: something banished is driven out, so that letter is removed from the word

parts.note: to bunk is to sleep in a bed, so bunked means occupied a bed
B is the abbreviation for bachelor

explanation.surface: A solitary single man is thrown out of a bed someone was already sleeping in.
explanation.walkthrough: BUNKED without its B leaves UNKED.
explanation.definitionFit: Unked is a dialect word from the north of England meaning lonely, dreary or desolate.

clue.text: Wicked activity showcased by irremediable Riefenstahl

indicators.note: a showcase displays its contents, so the answer is on display within the following words

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: Leni Riefenstahl's unforgivable propaganda films displayed evil deeds.
explanation.walkthrough: Leni Riefenstahl was a German film-maker notorious for Nazi propaganda, which makes 'wicked activity' sit naturally in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Diablerie means devilry or sorcery, mischief associated with devils and black magic.

clue.text: Unsettled area surrounding new estate in Paraíba

indicators.note: to surround something is to enclose it, so the outer letters wrap around one inner letter

parts.note: fazed means disconcerted or unsettled
A is the abbreviation for area
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A disputed district around a newly founded property in a Brazilian state.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unsettled' looks like an anagram signal, but it is a plain synonym, and area joins it before both go round new.
explanation.definitionFit: A fazenda is a large plantation or ranch in Brazil, and Paraíba is a Brazilian state.

clue.text: Grabbing spades, scrape up residue of retreating glacier

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means read from bottom to top, so the word runs backwards
to grab something is to take hold of it, so one letter ends up enclosed

parts.note: to rake is to scrape with a toothed tool
S is the abbreviation for spades in card games

explanation.surface: Someone with spades scrapes up what a glacier left behind as it melted back.
explanation.walkthrough: RAKE runs backwards as EKAR, which then takes in S: E(S)KAR.
explanation.definitionFit: An eskar, more often spelt esker, is a long ridge of gravel deposited by meltwater from a retreating glacier.

clue.text: To inspire older brother to cut English beef, say it

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for English

indicators.note: something that cuts into a word splits it, so those letters are placed inside

parts.note: beef is an example of meat
Br is a dated abbreviation for brother
in the playground chasing game, the chaser who is 'it' was traditionally called 'he'

explanation.surface: An elder sibling is asked to carve the beef, as an encouragement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' looks like padding at the end of the surface, but it is a piece: the child who chases in tag was once called 'he'.
explanation.definitionFit: To embreathe is an old word for breathing something into a person, which is what inspire literally means.

clue.text: Scottish cardinal excusing FA from religious legal judgment

indicators.note: to excuse someone is to let them off attending, so those letters are left out

parts.note: a fatwa is a ruling on a point of Islamic law
the Football Association, taken here simply as two letters to remove

explanation.surface: A Scottish Catholic cardinal pardons the Football Association from a religious ruling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' suggests a churchman, which suits the religious surface, but it means a cardinal number; FA is just the letters F and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Twa is the Scots form of two, and two is a cardinal number as opposed to an ordinal like second.

clue.text: Repeating this change would make sauna such a stinker

parts.note: the entry reads as 'A to K', an instruction to replace A by K
the instruction is applied to both A's in the word that follows, not just one
the word the change is applied to; with both A's turned to K it becomes the animal

explanation.surface: A recipe for turning a steamy sauna into something that reeks.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as 'A to K': swap each A in SAUNA for K and you get SKUNK, so the entry names its own creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The atok is a South American skunk, an animal famous for spraying a foul odour.

clue.text: Chipper article about Britain; in the same source, vegan diet item

indicators.note: about means around, so the first pieces go around the later ones

parts.note: an adze is a tool for chipping wood
an indefinite article
the United Kingdom
ib. is short for ibidem, Latin for 'in the same place', used in references

explanation.surface: A cheery newspaper piece on Britain recommends a plant-based food, citing the same reference.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chipper' reads as cheerful, but it is a tool that chips. The insertion goes inside the tool's name, not around the article.
explanation.definitionFit: Adzuki beans are small red pulses widely eaten by people following a plant-based diet.

clue.text: Dull purple beam spans shop

indicators.note: to span something is to stretch across it, so the outer word wraps round the inner one

parts.note: to beam is to smile broadly
a deli is a delicatessen shop

explanation.surface: A lavender-grey girder stretches across a store.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beam' reads as a girder, but it means a broad smile; GRI(DELI)N.
explanation.definitionFit: Gridelin is an old colour name for a greyish violet, from French gris de lin, flax grey.

clue.text: S African native plant used in cooking, its second half absorbing the first green light

indicators.text: its second half absorbing the first
indicators.note: the latter half of the word swallows its own front half, so the two halves are nested instead of side by side

parts.note: a herb is a plant used for flavouring food
giving the green light means saying OK

explanation.surface: A South African plant used in cookery is described oddly, then given the go-ahead.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the herb in two; its back half wraps around its front half, so the word is turned inside out.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhebok is a small grey antelope found only in southern Africa.

clue.text: What for contrary men ages old string instruments?

indicators.note: contrary means going the opposite way, so the preceding words are read backwards

parts.note: eh? asks what someone said
pro means in favour of
OR is other ranks, ordinary soldiers
eons are vast stretches of time

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about what ancient instruments contrary men played.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Contrary' seems to describe the men, but it acts on the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: The orpheoreon was a wire-strung plucked instrument of the cittern family used around 1600.

clue.text: Diminutive tunneller demolished raw eggs in thick sauce

indicators.note: in places the jumbled letters inside the outer word
something demolished is knocked to pieces, so the letters are broken up and rebuilt

parts.note: the seven letters reworked
a dip is a thick sauce for dunking food

explanation.surface: Raw eggs are smashed into a thick dip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Diminutive' belongs to the definition: digger wasps are small insects that burrow.
explanation.definitionFit: Digger wasps are small solitary insects that excavate burrows in soil to house their larvae.

clue.text: Common people injecting speed foolishly into knee

indicators.note: an injection puts something inside, so the scrambled letters go within the other word
acting foolishly means without sense or order, so those letters are scrambled

parts.note: the five letters reworked
genu is the anatomical Latin word for knee

explanation.surface: Ordinary folk stupidly inject amphetamines into their knees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speed' is drug slang in the surface but here is simply the letters to jumble; GEN(SDEPE)U.
explanation.definitionFit: Gens de peu is French for people of little account, the lower classes.

clue.text: Papa will look sideways for lost gunner

parts.note: Papa is P in the NATO phonetic alphabet
'is to' expresses what will happen, as in 'he is to leave'
to leer is to look sidelong, often slyly

explanation.surface: Dad will glance askance, searching for a missing gunman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lost' tells you the word is obsolete, a gunner of former times.
explanation.definitionFit: A pistoleer was a soldier or person armed with a pistol, a term now archaic.

clue.text: Peak half-visible on climber's route diagram

parts.note: the top is the summit

indicators.note: if a two-letter word is only half visible, just one of its letters can be seen

parts.note: only half of this two-letter word survives

explanation.surface: A mountain top partly showing on a climbing guide's sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' looks like a link word, but it is the word that is half-visible.
explanation.definitionFit: Climbers call a drawn diagram of a crag showing the lines of routes a topo, short for topographic.

clue.text: Backward idiot no longer, eh?

indicators.note: backward means facing the opposite way, so the word is read from end to start

parts.note: a nana is a silly person in British slang

explanation.surface: A slow-witted person is cured of stupidity, apparently.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backward' first reads as an insult alongside 'idiot'. 'No longer' marks the definition as an archaic expression.
explanation.definitionFit: Anan is an obsolete exclamation asking someone to repeat themselves, used like a puzzled 'pardon?'

clue.text: Quits last part of heptathlon after central switch?

indicators.note: the two letters in the very middle trade places, so the phrase changes only at its centre

parts.note: a heptathlon has seven events, so its last part is event seven

explanation.surface: An athlete gives up in the final heptathlon discipline after a mid-race change.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quits' looks like a verb about giving up, but it is the adjective for being square; swapping the middle T and S of EVENT SEVEN gives EVENS TEVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Being quits with someone means owing nothing either way, which is what even-steven expresses.

clue.text: Interrupting departure, copper had made this

indicators.note: to interrupt is to break into the middle of something, so these letters go inside

parts.note: an exit is a leaving
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
the 'd of the contraction I'd or he'd

explanation.surface: A policeman cut short someone's departure, having made it happen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' reads as a policeman, but it is the metal, and 'had' is the contracted 'd.
explanation.definitionFit: Excudit is Latin for 'struck or made it', inscribed after an engraver's or printer's name on a print.

clue.text: Ancient metric guide, universal among the ones with degrees

indicators.note: something among a group sits in its midst, so the single letter goes inside

parts.note: grads are graduates, people with degrees
U is the film certificate for universal viewing

explanation.surface: A classic measurement handbook is used by every graduate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Metric' suggests the metre as a unit of length, but here it means verse metre, the scansion of classical poetry.
explanation.definitionFit: A gradus was a dictionary of Latin or Greek prosody, a guide for schoolboys writing verse in ancient metres.

clue.text: N American rail industry's first to abandon party

indicators.note: to abandon is to leave behind, so that letter is dropped from the word

parts.note: a soirée is an evening party

indicators.note: first picks out only the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter of industry

explanation.surface: A North American railway company's founder walks out on a celebration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rail' reads as a railway, but it is the bird: SOIREE loses its I.
explanation.definitionFit: The soree, better known as the sora, is a small marsh bird of the rail family found in North America.

clue.text: Khan's hybrid fowl to complement "picken"?

indicators.note: a hybrid mixes two things, here grafting the change that turns one word into another onto this word

parts.note: poultry are domestic fowl
picken needs CH in place of P to become chicken, and the same swap is made here

explanation.surface: A khan breeds a crossbred bird to go alongside a chicken with a misprinted name.
explanation.walkthrough: Changing P to CH turns picken into chicken; doing the same to POULTRY gives CHOULTRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A khan is an inn for caravans, and a choultry is an Indian travellers' rest house or caravanserai.

clue.text: India's sweet man behaving immaturely over nothing

parts.note: a lad is a young man, especially one acting boisterously
O is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for over
O looks like zero

explanation.surface: A grown man acts childishly over some Indian confectionery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Over' reads as 'about', but it gives O, the cricket abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A ladoo is a round Indian confection made from flour, sugar and ghee, eaten at festivals.

clue.text: Tupelo gym hog's back, possibly after vitality

indicators.note: after places the final word's piece ahead of the rest, since the rest comes later

parts.note: pep is energy or liveliness
PE is physical education, school gym lessons
a hog's back is a long steep ridge; the Hog's Back in Surrey is one

explanation.surface: Elvis's home town gym, where a pig's rear end gets a lively workout.
explanation.walkthrough: Tupelo suggests the Mississippi town where Elvis was born, but it is the tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The pepperidge, or black gum, is a North American tree of the tupelo genus Nyssa.

clue.text: Seeing regular losses, redraft plot in Pretoria

indicators.note: suffering losses at regular intervals means every other letter goes missing

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters are kept

explanation.surface: After repeated setbacks, a scheme is rewritten in the South African capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' sounds like a scheme being redrafted, but it is a piece of land.
explanation.definitionFit: In South Africa an erf is a plot of land in a town, a building lot.

clue.text: Grass spliff to use as a drug outside broadcast

parts.note: to do a drug is to take it
OB is the standard abbreviation for an outside broadcast

explanation.surface: A cannabis joint is smoked outside a TV shoot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outside' looks like a container signal, but 'outside broadcast' is a single phrase, abbreviated OB.
explanation.definitionFit: Doob is slang for a joint, a hand-rolled cigarette of cannabis, which is also called grass.

clue.text: Corny Belgian cartoon character turned around anti-Euro manoeuvring

indicators.note: turned means facing the other way, so the name is read backwards
around means enclosing, so the outer word goes round the jumbled letters

parts.note: the Smurfs are little blue creatures created by the Belgian cartoonist Peyo

indicators.note: manoeuvring moves things into new positions, so those letters are rearranged

parts.note: the eight letters reworked

explanation.surface: A Belgian cartoon character campaigns against the European currency, which sounds hackneyed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corny' suggests trite, but it means relating to corn; SMURF reversed is FRUMS, which goes round the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Frumentarious means relating to corn or grain, from Latin frumentum, wheat.
